away.blurb: The ACC has issued the initial injury report for NC State football vs. Stanford for Friday night in Week 9. Along with the slew of season-ending injuries already known prior to the week, starters Duke Scott and Tristan Teasdell are officially out while Jojo Trader and Kamen Smith are questionable. RALEIGH, N.C. -- NC State starting running back Duke Scott will officially be out against Stanford after suffering an apparent leg/foot injury against Louisville on Saturday. He'll be joined by starting safety Tristan Teasdell , who was also listed as OUT along with several players suffering season-ending injuries like Spike Sowells, AJ Richardson, Vander Ploog and Yousef Mugharbil. The movement along the line highlights the injury concerns for the Wolfpack, with only two Week 0 starting linemen -- Teague Andersen and Jimarion McCrimon -- remaining in the trenches. If Kamen Smith can return after being listed as questionable for a second straight week, he would give the Pack a tremendous boost with names like Brody Smith and/or TK Whitset potentially needing to step up. away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

The Miami, Florida, native was rumored to be a top target for several schools looking for quarterbacks in his home state, but will return to an NC State team that will now have far higher aspirations following an 8-5 campaign that ended with wins in four of its past five games. picks.headline: Indiana’s Curt Cignetti gives prediction on Michigan starting QB, talks impressive Wolverines
picks.blurb: Defending national champion Indiana is coming off a 19-15 loss to Ohio State that easily could have gone the other way. Now, the Hoosiers will head north to take on Michigan at The Big House, with the Wolverines coming off a 21-18 victory over Penn State. “Out of the frying pan, into the fire, as we get ready for Michigan,” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti , the reigning back-to-back AP coach of the year, said at his Monday press conference. “Impressive team, especially on defense.” Michigan made a quarterback change from sophomore Bryce Underwood to freshman Tommy Carr at halftime of the win over the Nittany Lions, and head coach Kyle Whittingham has opted not to name a starter for this weekend’s game. “Really tough opponent this week, Michigan,” Cignetti said. “Made a quarterback change in the second half against Penn State. Gave them a shot in the arm, scored three second-half touchdowns to win the game. “Really impressed with their defense, their quickness, their tenacity, the way they play, play in and play out, the way they run to the ball. This is a top-flight defense. “Offensively, they’re got good running backs. Quarterback came in, played really well. The other quarterback has a cannon and can run, makes a lot of plays with his legs. So they’ll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. “It’ll be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row. “Looking forward here, not backward. And this will be a very tough challenge.” Here’s what else Cignetti said about Michigan heading into Saturday’s game: Indiana looking to get its run game going “Teams like Ohio State, Michigan, they don’t get up much rushing yardage. We did have some positive runs. We got into kind of a throw mode — I think we called 46 passes and 26 runs — which is very uncharacteristic of us. “It all starts up front. And we all want more consistent production and explosive plays. We haven’t gotten the explosive plays the last two weeks.” On if he will watch high school film on Tommy Carr “You can see what you need to see in the second half of Penn State, in my opinion, which I watched. “I’d assume it would be him. It could be two quarterbacks on the field at the same time. That would not surprise me. They did that at Utah. And the other guy can make plays. “Schematically, they didn’t change a whole lot in the second half.” On playing multiple physical games in a row with no bye week yet “We try to keep them healthy and fresh the best we can the entire season. At this point in the year, there might be a slight tweak, but not major.”

Michigan is now 4-2 on the season, while Indiana is 6-1. Despite the game being played at Michigan Stadium, the Wolverines will be an underdog next Saturday versus the Hoosiers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Michigan is a 7.5-point underdog against Indiana, with the over/under set at 7.5 points. While Michigan is an underdog, could this game actually be closer than expected? away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

But the win came with a cost. Quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an arm injury late in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit. He left the field before returning with a sling on his right arm. Following the game, OSU head coach Ryan Day confirmed that Sayin would miss "several weeks." The absence of last year's Heisman Trophy finalist presents a major challenge for the Buckeyes as they prepare for a demanding stretch of their schedule. Despite the injury, Ohio State improved to 6-1 with its victory over Indiana. They move back into the race for a College Football Playoff berth. A timely bye week offers the team an opportunity to regroup before facing No. 19 USC on the road for a Halloween affair. The Buckeyes will then host Oregon and No. 25 Northwestern in consecutive weeks. Without Sayin, Ohio State will rely more heavily on its defense and an improved rushing attack to remain competitive. However, the injury could also affect the Heisman Trophy race, particularly for star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. One of the leading contenders after an outstanding start to the season, Smith recorded four catches for 68 yards and a touchdown against Indiana. He now has 52 receptions for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns. Ohio State will navigate all the difficulties in the coming weeks and adjust to Sayin's absence. home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Here are all the injury details you need to know for this week’s contest. First off, it’s great to see both wide receiver Andrew Marsh and left guard Nate Efobi completely off the injury report heading into this game. They were both listed as probable earlier this week, so it was likely they would be good to play in this game. But you never know how injuries develop over the course of a week, so it’s reassuring to see them absent from the final report. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for a few other offensive lineman. Right tackle Andrew Sprague continues to be out as he deals with an undisclosed ailment. Right guard Brady Norton is also out for this week’s game. Center Jake Guarnera is also a game-time decision, which would be another pretty big blow to the offensive line. Additionally, senior tight end Zack Marshall is set to miss today’s game against the Nittany Lions. Marshall has not been on the injury report all week long, so it’s very interesting that he is now listed as out. Hopefully we learn more about why he wasbn’t able to suit up today during Kyle Whittingham’s postgame press conference. Finally, the defense at least appears to be healthy heading into this game. Also listed as questionable all week long, starting edge rushers Dom Nichols and John Henry Daley, as well as linebacker Aisea Moa, are nowhere to be seen on the injury report. picks.blurb: Auburn is ready to return to its home field after pulling off one of college football's most stunning upsets in Week 7 over then-No. 1 Georgia. Auburn won the turnover battle, 3-0, and ran the football efficiently, outgaining the Bulldogs, 192-113, in what was arguably its cleanest game of the season. LSU bounced back from Week 6's loss at Kentucky by shutting out then-No. 19 Mississippi State in Baton Rouge, 31-0. The Tigers took advantage of a Kamario Taylor-less Mississippi State squad, outgaining them, 379-291. This week marks the second straight week Auburn has had to prepare for a top SEC squad in terms of production. LSU is the SEC-best in total offense (504 yards per game), defense (256.4 yards allowed per game), first downs (28 per game), and passing (308 yards per game). The Bayou Bengals rank in the top five in several other categories, including points per game, points allowed per game, and time of possession. However, Auburn proved in Athens last week that stats do not matter and that being more physical can be enough to win. A key storyline to follow is the battle between two first-year head coaches, Alex Golesh and Lane Kiffin. Kiffin is 2-3 against Auburn as a head coach, and has won his last two games against the Tigers (2022 and 2023 at Ole Miss). Golesh has never faced Kiffin as a head coach. Another storyline is the rivalry renewal between two old-school SEC West teams. Auburn and LSU have not played since the 2023 season, and LSU leads the series, 30-24-1 over Auburn . home.headline: Georgia football injury report: Another starter ruled out for Auburn
home.blurb: Starting Georgia safety KJ Bolden is officially out for Saturday’s clash with Auburn in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry. In Friday’s SEC Availability Report , the Bulldogs downgraded Bolden from doubtful to out. Georgia ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion , sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear , junior running back Chauncey Bowens , junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green on Wednesday with the first report of the week. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Bolden came off the field slowly late in Georgia’s win over Alabama after tallying 7 tackles (3 solo), a half tackle for loss and a half sack. After the game, he was wearing a heavy wrap around his left calf muscle. Bolden’s streak of 34 straight games played to start his Georgia career is in jeopardy. He has started 19 of the last 20, missing one first half due to a targeting penalty in the previous game. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since. The Bulldogs and Tigers tee it up at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Georgia will enjoy its only bye of the season in Week 8.

home.headline: Georgia football injury report vs. Auburn
Georgia Injury Report Ahead of Auburn Game Reveals Troubling Reality with RB Room
home.blurb: As it turns out though, Kirby Smart's team is going to be a little bit banged up as they try to avoid a first home defeat against Auburn in more than two decades. As was the case last week, the running back room is going to be a bit thin. With the reporting around Chauncey Bowens as murky as ever, he has been ruled out for the second straight week and could wind up missing more time than that. Bowens is ruled out along with Isiah Canion, who has not seen much work this season. Thomas Blackshear is also out once again, but this is not a huge surprise. The bigger surprising thing is KJ Bolden being listed as questionable, potentially banged up from the Alabama game but dealing with an unknown injury. Georgia Injury Report Ahead of Auburn Game Reveals Troubling Reality with RB Room - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) MichaelBrauner Thu, October 15, 2026 at 1:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs are headed into another rivalry game this week against the Auburn Tigers , trying to make it 10 wins in a row in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. Reports from Pete Thamel of ESPN indicated that while Nate Frazier is not on the injury report, he was not last week either but still did not end up playing in the win over Alabama. Regardless, it looks like it could be a significant opportunity once again for guys like Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker to tote the rock and showcase the depth that Georgia has at the position. Given what the Dawgs proved against the Crimson Tide, they should be able to run the ball with success once again versus Auburn even without Bowens and likely Frazier as well. As Georgia tries to stay undefeated and keep the winning streak against Auburn alive, there is going to be serious urgency from this team to play as well as they did last week, which can often be difficult to replicate. If Gunner Stockton can keep up his strong level of play, this Dawgs team is going to be tough for anyone they face to have a real chance of winning. Once again though, he is going to be doing it with a little bit of a shorthanded running back room. As for what that means moving forward for the rest of the season, it remains to be seen, but Georgia certainly passed the first test with a depleted running back room. Time will tell if they can pass the next one as well.

picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff UCL live updates Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview NBA breakout candidates NFL Power Rankings Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. “Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?” said McElroy. “Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. “I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon.” “Tennessee's defense is amazing,” added McElroy. “They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks.” Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. ‘A lot of people just can't get behind this' – ESPN's Cole Cubelic makes it clear how he feels about Tennessee QB George MacIntyre after Alabama Tennessee sophomore George MacIntyre is 2-0 as the Volunteers' starting quarterback. picks.blurb: 'I really don't want to do this' - Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray predicts the winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator Toggle Mobile Navigation Home The Tennessee Vols will be looking for their first win in Columbia since 2020 on Saturday against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is set to take on South Carolina on Saturday in Columbia. The Vols are coming off an emotional win over Alabama. And that win over Alabama combined with Tennessee's poor track record in Williams-Brice Stadium (UT is 2-6 in its last eight games in Columbia) has led to the Vols being put on upset alert this weekend by, well, almost everyone. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, picked South Carolina to beat Tennessee 27-24 . Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray, who is also an ESPN analyst, is making a similar prediction. Murray has South Carolina beating Tennessee 24-21. “So it comes down to picking this football game,” said Murray. “I really don't want to do this. I wish I could just not do it, but I've got to. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21. I'm doing it because I love both teams. And what have we learned this year? Teams coming off an emotional win do not perform well the next week. Tennessee's coming off an emotional win. South Carolina's coming off a bye. The game is in South Carolina. You fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. We've been doing this all year. It feels like every big time game in college football, the winner loses the next week — especially if it's on the road.” “I love both teams,” added Murray. “… I'm just going with what history has told us this season. Tennessee had an emotional win against Bama. Smoking those cigars all night does not bode well for [recovery] the next day. So they're going on the road. South Carolina's healthy and coming off the bye. South Carolina wins.” I'm sure there will be some analysts here and there who pick Tennessee to win this game, but it seems like the majority of folks are picking South Carolina to come out on top. Tennessee has a big concern that's quietly developing and no one's talking about it, but it could be a big problem by the end of the season Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers have a potential problem quietly developing this season. The Sooners were in control of the Wildcats for most of the game before their offense fell apart late. OU is dealing with a plethora of offensive line injuries and John Mateer's turnover issues reappeared against UK. This week, the Sooners hit the road again. "We've got to get off the mat and got to go to Starkville," OU coach Brent Venables said. "It's a very unforgiving league." The Sooners travel to face Mississippi State on Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium. The game will be the first-ever meeting between the two programs. Bulldogs coach Jeff Lebby served as OU's offensive coordinator for two seasons from 2022-2023. In Year 3 at the helm, Lebby's two SEC wins through four conference games are already the most of his tenure. Before injuring his foot in a win over Missouri and playing through visible pain against Alabama, Taylor was a legit Heisman Trophy contender. The sophomore has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. But he didn't play in this past Saturday's loss to LSU. His status will be the biggest storyline this week. The case for Mississippi State: If Taylor and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell return from injury, Lebby's offense should get back to its high-flying ways. And if the Bulldogs' defense can force John Mateer, who has turned the ball over nine times in six games, into mistakes they should win. away.blurb: "We had plenty of opportunities there late into the third quarter to knock them out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. Multiple injuries on the offensive line were a critical factor in the team's late-game collapse. Offensive lineman Ryan Fodje played through an injury, allowing two sacks on a key fourth-quarter drive. Quarterback John Mateer threw three interceptions, including a costly pick-six with just over a minute remaining. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. away.headline: Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley
away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

away.headline: Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game
away.blurb: Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Story by The Topeka Capital Journal Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads MANHATTAN — Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson returned to the game after missing one play that resulted in a touchdown. The quarterback was slow to get up after a 59-yard run that set up a four-yard rushing touchdown by Rodney Fields. Backup Jacob Knuth entered the game to hand the ball off to Fields with 13:46 left in the first quarter. Johnson lay on the turf for several minutes before being pulled up by the trainers. He smiled as he got up and had no noticeable limp . At the end of the 59-yard run, he stumbled before falling to the turf. Kansas ' Bryson Hayes returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven with 13:04 left in the opening quarter. On Johnson's first play back, he completed a 45-yard pass to a wide-open Derrick Salley downfield. The Wildcats ran a designed run for Johnson two plays later. picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. away.blurb: Brody Meadows' Potential Return Could Bolster Virginia Tech's Injury-Hit Offensive Line Skip to main content SI.COM BLACKSBURG — Virginia Tech 's offensive line has been dealt a great deal of change due to several injuries, which has left younger players to take on larger roles. As the Hokies look to find stability up front, the potential return of fifth-year senior Brody Meadows could provide a much-needed presence. The outlook on Meadows' return is trending in the right direction, according to head coach James Franklin, who said Wednesday that the veteran lineman could factor into Saturday's game against Georgia Tech . With Virginia Tech working through injuries to Justin Terry, Johnny Garrett and Montavious Cunningham along the offensive line, Franklin emphasized the value of having an experienced lineman available. Franklin mentioned that the coaching staff has been cautious with Meadows' return as the injury has continued to linger. However, Meadows is listed as probable on Wednesday's avalibility report ahead of Saturday's game against Georgia Tech. Franklin also said Meadows performed well in practice Wednesday and could factor into the offensive line rotation. "It wasn't just like telling the coach what he wants to hear," Franklin said. "I think he's excited about the opportunity to go out and help his team. So, you know, guys like that are invaluable." With Meadows listed as probable and younger lineman continuing to gain experience, Virginia Tech could have another experienced presence available up front against Georgia Tech. More from Virginia Tech Hokies On SI FOOTBALL Meadows, a 6-foot-7, 330-pound lineman from Bluefield, Va., has played in 28 games across his career. After missing the entire 2025 season due to a foot injury, Meadows returned to the field this season before suffering another injury in the first half against Boston College in week four. Through four games this season, Meadows has played 73 snaps and recorded a 66.6 overall offensive grade from Pro Football Focus. He has earned a 65.0 pass-blocking grade and a 66.5 run-blocking grade. "We may get Brody Meadows back, and Brody's played a lot of football, so, you know, there's a ton of value in that," Franklin said Wednesday. Beyond his experience on the field, Franklin had high praises for Meadows' attitude and the relationships he has built within the program. "I'm a huge fan of his," Franklin said. "He's well liked and respected by his teammates and the coaches." Franklin said he checked in with Meadows about how he was feeling Wednesday and was encouraged by the lineman's response. After practice, Meadows told Franklin he felt "fantastic," responding with a smile that coach believed was genuine. At a massive 6-foot-7 and 330 pounds, Meadows also brings size and length that is needed to compete along an ACC offensive line. away.blurb: Georgia Tech star RB Justice Haynes is doubtful for Virginia Tech. pic.twitter.com/KSfHWtT1QV On Wednesday night, the initial injury report for the game was released, and a couple of other names popped up for the Yellow Jackets, this time on offense. The Yellow Jackets' two running backs, Malachi Hosley and Justice Haynes, were both listed on the report, with Hosley already being ruled out and Haynes listed as doubtful. Haynes has 462 yards rushing this season on 87 carries and three touchdowns. Again, Haynes is doubtful, but you can bet that James Franklin and Brent Pry are still going to game plan for him just in case he's upgraded in the injury reports later this week before kickoff. If both are out, this is an opportunity that the Hokies must take advantage of and there would be no excuse for losing to Georgia Tech. Duke transfer wide receiver and punt returner Que'Sean Brown joined Reynolds, landing on an award watch list at the midway point of the season as well. home.headline: Dabo talks Clemson’s shutout win vs. Charleston Southern, updates injuries
home.blurb: “I’ve been around here a minute, and we’ve had some games like this over the years where I’m not real happy in the fourth quarter because we’re sloppy. You’re playing a bunch of guys (backups), and all of a sudden you lose your edge a little bit. I felt they never lost their edge. They played tough. It’s hard to shut people out.” “It’s hard to shut people out. They had three yards in the second half, and we played 90 guys or more, so played a lot of guys. I thought they (the backups) just kept showing up.” “We’re a work in progress. ... Devarrick Woods (who didn’t dress Saturday due to injury) is gonna help us. ... Kourtney Kelly was so happy to be out there again, and I think Vic Burley had his best game. He played stout.” “I’d just come out of the tunnel to go to the bus, and I saw those F-16s (flyover planes) coming. home.blurb: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return That progress includes moving from the larger brace to a sleeve and pad. Vizzina is still working to regain his full range of motion, so Swinney's update stops short of confirming a return to game action. True freshman Tait Reynolds took over as Clemson 's starter ahead of the North Carolina game after Vizzina started the first two contests. Vizzina was completely unavailable against the Tar Heels, then dressed against Cal strictly as an emergency option. Swinney made clear just how limited that availability was. Clemson would have turned to Trent Pearman and likely Brock Bradley before asking Vizzina to play against the Golden Bears. This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings Drew Landon, Clemson Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Christopher Vizzina has not played since suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern in Week 2. His recovery has taken longer than Clemson initially expected, but head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging update following Wednesday's practice. "CV is still not 100%, but this has been the best week he's had since before he got hurt," Swinney said. "He's just gotten better and better. We thought it would bounce back a little bit quicker, but it's just been hard for him," Swinney said. "But he's gotten better. He's had a really good week, and it's just one of those things that's been day-to-day." "It would have been like we would have had to get through Trent and probably even through Brock before we got to him," Swinney said. "He was just still really, really sore." Through his two starts, Vizzina completed 14 of 23 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. picks.headline: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch
picks.blurb: “They’re Going to Condense”: Former UCLA HC Predicts Trouble for Texas vs Ole Miss as Arch Manning’s Issues are Set to Force Tactical Switch - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff UCL live updates Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview NBA breakout candidates NFL Power Rankings Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning warms up before a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. © Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Prateek Singh Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:41 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Arch Manning's struggles against the Florida Gators have put the Texas Longhorns in a difficult position ahead of their matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday. Manning threw for 173 yards, completed 14 of 20 passes, and threw one touchdown. According to former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel, Texas will need to make key adjustments to its strategy ahead of the upcoming game. During an appearance on CBS Sports, Neuheisel picked Ole Miss to win. "I'm concerned for Texas in this game, not because I don't think they'll play hard and be geared up to play their best game of the season, but I feel like because of all the pressure on Arch, they're going to condense, and condensing will not be the answer to going against Pete Golding defense," he said . Neuheisel pointed out that Arch Manning attempted just 20 passes against Florida, arguing that such an approach will not be effective against the Ole Miss Rebels. While the Texas Longhorns have won four of their six games this season, Manning has shown only flashes of brilliance rather than the consistency expected of him. Overall, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns, and five interceptions. After his performance against the Gators, speculation began that he could be benched for the upcoming game. However, head coach Steve Sarkisian made it clear that Arch Manning will remain the team's starting quarterback. "There's no doubt about it, Arch can play better for us, but he's our starter," he said , per Fox Sports. "We need to see a better version of him this week." Sarkisian said Manning is a quality player and that, as a coach, it is his job to bring out the best in him on the field. Former Texas Coach Heaps Praise on Arch Manning On an episode of THE STAMPEDE, former Texas coach Mack Brown said Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorns are playing under immense pressure. He believes the team needs to free itself from that pressure before stepping onto the field. In Brown's view, Manning has the talent and ability to help get Texas back on track. "Arch's gotta go back and be the Arch we saw at the last of last year," he said. "He's good enough, he's athletic enough, he's smart enough, and for a 22-year-old, he has handled this pressure so well." Brown said the upcoming matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels will be crucial for the Longhorns and could shape their chances of making the College Football Playoff this season. By Braden Ramsey Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 1:46 PM EDT There are only two ranked-on-ranked matchups on the Week 8 college football slate. While Houston-Utah will draw plenty of eyeballs, the SEC will be locked in on Ole Miss-Texas in Austin. The Rebels (5-1, 3-1 SEC) have only one ranked foe on their schedule after this battle with the Longhorns. If they can handle business on the road, they will feel very secure in their College Football Playoff positioning. Meanwhile, the Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) would be all but eliminated from the CFP chase if they suffered a third consecutive defeat. ESPN's Greg McElroy broke down the matchup on his Always College Football program. He believes Ole Miss becomes a real SEC Championship contender with a victory. “If Ole Miss wins, the national narrative is that Ole Miss is a real SEC title contender… they would be 4-1 in the league,” McElroy said. “Here's the detail that makes Ole Miss very dangerous: they don't play Kentucky or Tennessee this year… when Georgia comes to Oxford on Nov. 7, that game is essentially a play-in for Atlanta.” On the other side of the coin, McElroy thinks a Texas loss is something the nation is salivating about. A win, though, would thrust them back into the CFP picture because of their early season triumphs against Ohio State and Tennessee. “For Texas, a loss is the story the whole country has just been waiting to write… [and] the conference title's gone in October,” McElroy claimed. “If Texas wins, the national narrative is, ‘the most dangerous two-loss team in the country just reminded everybody why [they're dangerous]'… you beat Ole Miss… you now have three teams that you've beaten all power rated in the top 12.” Hear more from McElroy here: The Rebels and Longhorns kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night (ABC). picks.headline: No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss opponent preview: Rebels head to Austin for first matchup as conference foes
picks.blurb: No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss opponent preview: Rebels head to Austin for first matchup as conference foes | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 21, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football A talented Rebels team comes to Austin for a top-25 matchup on Saturday. With a 5-1 record and Top 10 ranking, the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels head to Austin on Saturday to face off against a struggling Texas Longhorns team that dropped to No. 19 in the AP Top 25 after consecutive losses to unranked opponents. The first matchup between the two foes in 13 years, Saturday’s battle is the first as conference opponents with the Longhorns leading the all time series 6-2. After a deep College Football Playoff run to the semifinals last season also featured controversy with former head coach Lane Kiffin, Ole Miss and first-year head coach Pete Golding are continuing that success — the Rebels already have three ranked wins and have bounced back with consecutive wins after getting beaten by Florida. The Rebels boast one of the most prolific passing attacks in the SEC behind star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who is joined by an elite duo in running back Kewan Lacy and wide receiver Deuce Alexander. Defensively, Ole Miss has been inconsistent, giving up 40-plus points in two matchups, but also holding multiple conference opponents to under 20 points. Golding was promoted from the defensive coordinator position, giving his team a clear identity and scheme continuity that isn’t traditional for first-year head coaches. The matchup on Saturday is the biggest road test for the Rebels and yet another litmus test of whether Ole Miss will be a national title contender this year. Here’s how the Rebels stack up position by position. Ole Miss has one of the most experienced and dangerous quarterbacks in the nation in Trinidad Chambliss, who has been electric after taking over the starting role during the middle of last season, currently ranking third in the Heisman Trophy odds at FanDuel. Through six games, he has accumulated 1,676 yards on a 67.6 completion percentage with 14 touchdowns and four interceptions. However, Chambliss does his best work when navigating the pocket. His ability to extend plays and use his legs makes him extremely difficult to defend. You can’t just get pressure on him, you must maintain rush-lane integrity and perhaps even devote a spy to defending him, otherwise he will make plays with his legs. Facing one of the sports biggest stars, the Texas defense has a monumental challenges on Saturday. The priority has to be making the offense one dimensional and maintaining discipline when rushing the passer. Joining Chambliss in the backfield is another star in running back Kewan Lacy. A year ago, Lacy was recognized as an All-American behind his 1,567 rushing yards and 24 touchdowns. Through five games, with one missed due to injury, he has recorded 352 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.7 yards per attempt. Lacy has shown to be tough and injury-prone. He missed a game earlier this season thanks to a shoulder injury and was banged up against Missouri with a lower-body issue. However, neither stopped him. Despite missing most of the second quarter last Saturday, he still rushed for a season-high 122 yards on 16 carries. If Lacy can manage to play the full game on Saturday, he is lethal and will be playing with an extra chip on his shoulder. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home,” Lacey said. “It’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” The Lancaster product was a Texas fan during his childhood and actually wanted to become a Longhorn, but he ended up signing with Missouri after Texas failed to extend an offer in the 2024 recruiting cycle, signing Jerrick Gibson and Christian Clark instead. “I wanted to commit to UT,” Lacy said at SEC Media Days in July. “That was my dream my freshman year, I wanted to go to Texas. But my process throughout my high school career, I never really got an opportunity from them.” Come Saturday, Lacy will have a huge opportunity to showcase what the Longhorns missed out on. If he can’t go, the Rebels will turn to transfer Mekhi Frazier and freshman JT Lindsey to handle the load. Frazier arrived on campus this past season after leading Michigan State in rushing yards last year. He’s recorded 254 yards on 45 carries this season. Wide receiver The leading threat in the pass game is Deuce Alexander, but the Rebels possess a deep and talented wide out room with plenty of players that can help move the ball. Alexander caught 44 passes for 684 yards and two touchdowns last year behind second-round draft pick De’Zhaun Stribling, while adding 122 yards on the ground. This season as WR1, he’s nearly reached that mark halfway through the year with 35 catches for 523 yards and five touchdowns. At 14.9 yards per catch, Alexander is a downfield threat that can generate chunk plays in a hurry. He started his career in the slot but has emerged as a player that can use his speed from any point on the field. His top-end speed is elite and forces the defense to shade over to prevent the deep ball. Behind Alexander are Traylon Ray and Horatio Fields, who have combined for 39 catches and 509 yards this season. Ray is another downfield option while Fields is a more reliable target that can shoulder the load when defenses prioritize Alexander and Ray. Former Longhorn Johntay Cook is also on the roster and has recorded eight catches for 74 yards and a score. Tight end Caleb Odom is another reliable threat for Chambliss. In five games, he’s tallied 21 catches for 267 yards and two touchdowns, which slots him second on the team in receptions. Odom is a drive-extending pass catcher. At 12.7 yards per reception and a season long of 35 yards, he’s not going to decimate a defense down the field, but rather provide Chambliss with an intermediate option. Most importantly, Odom can attack the middle of the field and provide matchup problems when opposing defense are forced to prioritize Alexander or stack the box to stop Lacy. The 6’5, 245-pound junior is in his second season at Ole Miss after appearing in 12 games for Alabama as a freshman in 2024. He’s stepped up dramatically after seeing just a handful of targets last year and has positioned himself as a legitimate threat this season. If you can somehow stop the run, minimize Chambliss’ legs, and cover the wideouts, Odom can decimate you on quick passes and intermediate throws. Offensive line The Ole Miss offensive line comes to Austin riding high after one of the best performances of the season last week. The Rebels ran for 257 yards while averaging 6.7 yards per carry last week, and the front five as a whole graded as the highest unit in the country, according to Pro Football Network. Heading into the year, the offensive line had holes to fill thanks to two NFL departures. A host of transfers were brought in and have done a solid job in six games. Leading the way is right guard Patrick Kutas, while left tackle Terez Davis is another steady presence on the other side of the line. Disrupting the line up front will be key to stopping the run and disrupting Chambliss. If Texas can win up front without needing to stack the box, the Longhorn defense will be in a good spot. As a whole, the offense for Ole Miss can attack a defense in a variety of ways. With elite skill position players that can rack up huge plays and one of the best quarterbacks in the country, the Longhorn defense has their work cut out for them. Winning individual battles will be key on Saturday. With a multi-dimensional offense that can attack you in so many different ways, Muschamp will need to pick and choose who he leaves on an island and hope that they succeed. The defense is headed by Bryan Brown, who is the sole defensive coordinator after sharing the role with Golding before Golding’s promotion. Though Brown is the defensive coordinator, this unit is heavily influenced by Golding, who likes to use a mix of twists and stunts to create pressure and stop the run game up front. This year, the unit has been middle of the pack in conference play. The unit suffocated Missouri and Vanderbilt, but also gave up 52 to Florida. Running the ball has proven most effective against Ole Miss, a part of the game Texas hasn’t looked exceptional at. Here are the key Rebels to keep an eye on. Defensive line Leading the charge up front is defensive tackle Will Echoles, an established disruptor. As a sophomore last season, Echoles was recognized as first-team All-SEC, according to the AP, after registering five sacks, 11.5 tackles for loss, and 68 total tackles. According to Pro Football Focus, he led the Power Four in pressures and defensive stops. When Echoles isn’t getting pressure, he utilizes his hands very well. Last season, he batted down the ninth-most passes among all defensive linemen in college football. This season, he’s already gotten off to a hot start with 18 tackles and 1.5 sacks. He will undoubtedly impact the game so ensuring Echoles doesn’t do so routinely will be key for the Longhorn offense. On the edge, Cam Franklin and Blake Purchase can disrupt plays if not blocked properly. Purchase leads the team with 3.5 sacks while also adding 23 tackles and a forced fumble. He shined against Vanderbilt with a two-sack performance. If the Longhorns can’t keep a clean pocket, the Texas offense will struggle. The Ole Miss front four isn’t the most talented in the conference, but still has more than enough players to attack inside or on the edge. The teeth of the defense is the linebacker room. Led by Suntarine Perkins with heavy contributions from Luke Ferrelli, Keaton Thomas, and Tah’j Butler, this group is the best unit in Golding’s defense. Perkins is a hybrid-style player with great speed and athleticism. He’s good in coverage and can rush the passer. Two years ago he recorded 10.5 sacks for the Rebels. Ferrelli is the leading tackler for the Rebels and has become a great piece for Golding after a controversial offseason in which Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney accused Golding of tampering after Ferrelli committed to the Tigers, but changed his mind and opted to join Golding. Originally at Cal, Ferrelli was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year last season and has continued that success with a team leading 39 tackles in addition to two sacks. Thomas has been strong against the run and in tackling but has struggled in pass coverage, something Texas can exploit come Saturday. As a whole, the linebackers have experience, top end talent, and depth making them an important part of the Ole Miss defense. Cornerback Jaylon Braxton and safety Joenel Aguero are the two premier defenders on the back end. Braxton lines up on the outside opposite of Antonio Kite, the other corner for the Rebels. Braxton is an experienced defender and will flash his hat tackling. He’s got 23 tackles and an interception to his name this year. While he will give up catches, he does a good job limited yardage. Meanwhile, Kite brings a veteran presence after starting 12 games for Ole Miss last year. He’s had a solid year, grading at 69.9 in coverage according to Pro Football Focus. Playing free safety, Aguero is a versatile defender in his first season at Ole Miss after spending three season as a Georgia Bulldog in which he appeared in 35 games including starting all 12 last season. away.headline: Ole Miss-Missouri injury update: Key players’ statuses heading into Saturday
away.blurb: The most important news from this week's Student-Athlete Availability Reports for No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss was included in the initial report with Rebels defensive back Edwin Joseph listed as out for Saturday's matchup. Since then, there hasn't been much movement on either side, and Thursday night's updated report was largely status quo. The only notable change for Ole Miss was reserve offensive lineman Enoch Wangoy being added to the out list. While Wangoy has not been a regular contributor this season, his addition pushes the Rebels' total number of unavailable players to nine. Injuries have tested depth charts across the SEC all season, and Ole Miss is no exception. Fortunately for the Rebels, most of the players listed as out have been absent for several weeks, allowing the coaching staff time to adjust rotations and personnel packages. Ole Miss also continues to have just one player listed as questionable in tight end Hayden Bradley, while defensive backs Antonio Kite, MJ Preston and Ladarian Clardy remain listed as probable. If those three are able to play, it would help offset some of the losses in the secondary caused by Joseph and Nascar McCoy being unavailable. Missouri's report had six players listed as out, including running back Ahmad Hardy and safety JaDon Blair. Two more players are listed as doubtful, while linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. and defensive tackle Sterling Webb remain questionable. Perhaps the most interesting names on Missouri's report are former Ole Miss players Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee . Both are listed as probable entering the weekend and appear to be trending toward availability for Saturday's game. It would not be surprising to see either player removed from the report on Friday or prior to kickoff as Missouri prepares for one of the SEC's featured matchups this weekend. away.headline: Is Kewan Lacy Playing Today? Ole Miss RB Injury News vs. Former Team Mizzou
away.blurb: If the injuries were bad enough, of course, they could still hold Lacy out. But if he was healthy, he'd definitely want to get out on the field and play. Given the talent level on the field on Saturday, Ole Miss will likely need more out of Lacy. It worked out as well as anyone could've imagined. He ran for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns last season. Ole Miss Bounces Back vs. Vanderbilt Behind Star RB’s Return Trinidad Chambliss Injury Update: Did Ole Miss QB Return vs. Florida? Is Kewan Lacy Playing Today? Ole Miss RB Injury News vs. Former Team Mizzou Kewan Lacy wasn't going to want to miss this one. Ole Miss running back has battled injuries this season, but Saturday brings a clash with his former program, the Missouri Tigers . So now that the day has arrived, what's the scoop? We've got the details here. Yes, Kewan Lacy is slated to play on Saturday for Ole Miss against Mizzou. He wasn't on the injury report at all this week, clearing him to be on the field for a game against his former squad. Lacy did play last week against Vanderbilt, but he ran just seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown before the Rebels let him rest down the stretch of that one. Lacy has played in four games so far this season, running 46 times for 230 yards and five touchdowns. A season ago, Lacy was one of the best RBs in the country as Ole Miss made a run to the College Football Playoff. If they want another CFP run this season, it'll likely start by picking up a key ranked win on Saturday against Missouri. Lacy's final two choices in high school were Ole Miss and Missouri, according to Sports Illustrated . He went with the Tigers originally, heading there for his freshman season in 2024. Lacy didn't see much work — just 23 runs for 104 yards. He didn't find the end zone. So after that year, he entered the transfer portal and went the do-over route. He chose Ole Miss this time, flipping to the other side of his original recruitment decision. This season, Mizzou currently has had the more productive RB, as Jamal Roberts is putting together a big year while injuries have held Lacy back. But the matchup on Saturday may be exactly what Lacy needs to get rolling into the second half of this season. It always adds a little bit of extra motivation to face off with some old friends. home.blurb: Texas football has not played well over the past two weeks, and there’s a good chance that Arch Manning will be benched as KJ Lacey Jr. is expected to take some first-team reps this week. As much as Simmons’ injury is a serious topic, everyone is still looking at the Manning situation in shock. He was slated to be one of the top quarterbacks going into the draft next year, and if he actually gets benched, his stock could take a big hit. There could even be a scenario where he decides to return to Texas for another year. picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff UCL live updates Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview NBA breakout candidates NFL Power Rankings Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week.
