Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. home.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky's playoff outlook?
home.blurb: Baxter was listed as a game-time decision on the pre-Oklahoma availability report. He participated in warmups and was running sprints on the sideline throughout the game but didn’t actually play. If Baxter does experience any setbacks this week, it does feel like holding him out against Vanderbilt with a bye week to follow would be a wise choice since Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes can still carry the load at running back. Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. The injuries for backup linebacker Antwan Smith and backup nickel back Jaden Smith appear to be long-term issues, so do not expect them back soon. Wide receiver Nic Anderson’s status will be worth watching this week too after he appeared to reaggravate his arm/shoulder issue in Oklahoma. For most of the history of Kentucky football winning in the home stadium of a traditional power like Oklahoma would have been the high point of a season. Jackson Williams caught five balls for 58 yards in the victory. New Mexico Lobos Betting Preview Over on the Lobos’ side, they also have just one blemish on their schedule so far. New Mexico beat Central Michigan and Mercyhurst in their first two games ahead of a tough 14-6 loss to Oklahoma. The Lobos have since been on a tear, taking out New Mexico State, UTEP and Hawaii over the last three games on the way to a 5-1 overall run. Matched up against Hawaii last weekend the Lobos were down 10-0 by the end of the first half. New Mexico began their comeback with a TD in the third, then added two more trips to the end zone on the way to a 21-10 victory in the end. QB Toa Fa’avae was 5-of-10 for 59 yards and two picks. Scottre Humphrey had 15 carries for 90 yards and two scores. North Dakota State Bison Player Prop Facts Heading into Week 8, Marion Moore ranks T3rd amongst FBS players for interceptions (4) this season. Matchup/League Facts New Mexico ranks 1st among FBS teams for points allowed per game this season (10.5). New Mexico has recorded the equal-most home wins by a margin of 40+ points of any FBS team this season (2). North Dakota State has won the second quarter in each of its last eight games – longest active streak in the FBS. North Dakota State ranks 2nd among FBS teams for points allowed per game this season (11.3). New Mexico vs North Dakota State Prediction I’ll stick with New Mexico but you could call this one either way. The Lobos played an ugly game versus Hawaii, bagging three turnovers and 16 penalties for 145 yards. New Mexico mustered just 94 yards passing, 5-of-13 on third downs and 16 first downs but the defense kept the team from imploding with 3-of-13 on third downs and two takeaways. New Mexico has 21 or more points in all five of their wins this year and 38 or more in four of them. As for North Dakota State, they held Nevada to just 15 first downs and 286 total yards with two takeaways in their latest win. The Bison defense has been great this year, giving up 17 points or fewer in six of seven games. This matchup could go a lot of different ways and it’ll be a fun one to watch. home.headline: New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck out for 'a while' after suffering shoulder injury
home.blurb: Multiple Lobos listed as out or questionable for Saturday's game against Hawaii UNM’s Jaxton Eck (6) gets ready for the next play during a scrimmage at University Stadium in Albuquerque NM on August 15, 2026. Mike Sandoval/Journal Sean Reider Sean Reider Journal Staff Writer Published October 15, 2026 - 12:01 p.m. Modified October 15, 2026 - 2:34 p.m. New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck will be out for “a while” after breaking a bone in his shoulder, head coach Jason Eck told the Journal on Thursday. The 6-foot-1, 228-pound senior did not practice this week and was observed with his arm in a sling before he was ruled out for Saturday’s game at Hawaii. Jason Eck said the preseason Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year’s bone break is in the same shoulder he hurt in the Rate Bowl on Dec. 27. Eck added that he does not believe Jaxton’s injury is season-ending, but expects him to miss an extended period of time. His designation was first released via an initial availability report from the Mountain West on Thursday, one that saw multiple key Lobos listed as out or questionable ahead of Saturday’s game. Late to seeing this: LB Jaxton Eck and CB Frankie Edwards III are OUT for Saturday’s game. WR Massiah Mingo and RB Kiefer Sibley are also questionable. https://t.co/5jqZVKeiZ5 Only one Lobo was newly ruled out for the rest of the season on the initial report: backup linebacker Nick Wheeler, who Eck said suffered a torn ACL. Without Jaxton and Wheeler, UNM is expected to rely on linebackers Mercury Swaim and Clay Martineau for the near future. Starting cornerback Frankie Edwards III (9 total tackles) has also been ruled out for Saturday’s game, per the league’s availability report. Eck said the 5-10, 178-pound junior suffered a concussion, and expects him to return as soon as next week. Wide receiver Massiah Mingo (ankle) and running back Kiefer Sibley (shoulder) are questionable for Saturday’s game, per the availability report. A 5-9, 170-pound freshman, Mingo has caught five passes for 56 yards; Sibley has rushed for 205 yards, the second-best mark on the team.
